validated_results.title: Diet and vitamin or mineral supplements and risk of renal cell carcinoma in Canada.
authors: Canadian Cancer Registries Epidemiology Research Group
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting adjusted odds ratios for red meat items (hamburger, sausage, beef/pork/lamb as main dish) and incident histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma.

extraction.comparison_type: highest level versus lowest level of hamburger consumption
extraction.population: Newly diagnosed histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma cases and population controls in eight Canadian provinces

sample_size.excerpt: Mailed questionnaires were completed by 1279 (691 male and 588 female) newly diagnosed histologically confirmed RCC cases and 5370 (2696 male and 2674 female) population controls between 1994 and 1997 in eight Canadian provinces. Measurement included information on socioeconomic status, smoking habits, alcohol use, diet, and vitamin or mineral supplements.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 1279 + 5370 = 6649

cases.excerpt: Mailed questionnaires were completed by 1279 (691 male and 588 female) newly diagnosed histologically confirmed RCC cases and 5370 (2696 male and 2674 female) population controls between 1994 and 1997 in eight Canadian provinces.

effect_size.excerpt: An increased risk was observed (for males and females combined) with increased consumption of hamburger and sausage: adjusted ORs for highest level versus lowest level were 1.4 (95% CI = 1.1-1.8) and 1.5 (95% CI = 1.2-2.0), respectively, p = 0.003 and 0.01. Beef, pork or lamb as a main dish and processed meats were also associated with increased RCC.

confidence_interval.excerpt: An increased risk was observed (for males and females combined) with increased consumption of hamburger and sausage: adjusted ORs for highest level versus lowest level were 1.4 (95% CI = 1.1-1.8) and 1.5 (95% CI = 1.2-2.0), respectively, p = 0.003 and 0.01.
